newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GERMANY CONFIDENT OF DEPOSING UKRAINE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANY CONFIDENT OF DEPOSING UKRAINE.

text.p: Confident European champions Germany plan to depose Ukraine and take their rightful place at the top of their World Cup qualifying group nine on Saturday despite the loss of experienced midfielder Andreas Moeller to injury.
Germany coach Berti Vogts has decided not to worry about replacing the 29-year-old Moeller, who helped Borussia Dortmund to victory in the European Cup final last week but now has a knee injury.

Vogts, whose side beat Ukraine 2-0 at home at the end of April, will travel to Kiev on Friday with a 20-man squad knowing a win would put them one point clear in the group with a game in hand and their toughest matches behind them.
Ukraine's coach Jozhef Sabo is less sanguine. He said on Thursday he had eight players injured.
Casualties include Dynamo Kiev midfielder Vitaly Kosovsky, who is having surgery on his leg on Friday.
Odessa Chornomorets striker Timerlan Guseinov, one of Ukraine's top scorers, is also carrying a leg injury

"The situation now is very difficult. We were forced to ask Dynamo Kiev urgently to provide players. At least 16 players are needed for normal training sessions and I didn't have enough. But now the mood is good and everyone wants to play," Sabo said.
Portugal, who lie third in the group two points behind Germany, could do with a confidence-boosting big win over bottom team Albania in Oporto.
But the Portuguese risk losing Barcelona's Luis Figo for the match, further weakening a midfield already depleted by injury to Fiorentina's Rui Costa.
Figo was forced to abandon training on Wednesday because of a slight muscle strain. Squad officials say he is responding well to treatment and hope he will be able to make the team.

Surprise group five leaders Israel arrived in Moscow early on Thursday for their toughest challenge of the competition to date on Sunday. Israel whose home tie against Russia last October produced a 1-1 draw are two points ahead of the Russians but have played one game more.

Coach Shlomo Scharf, who has dropped three players -- Avishai Janno and Assi Domb due to lack of fitness and Ronen Harazi because of lack of match practice -- said he intended to field a defensive line-up with Ronnie Rosenthal probably being given a role of attacking midfielder.
"I would be happy to come away with a 0-0 draw," he told reporters before leaving Tel Aviv.

Bulgaria, third in the group two points behind Russia but with a game in hand, should have little trouble at home to Luxembourg after healing a rift between Bulgarian officials and top player Hristo Stoichkov.
"The atmosphere in the squad is normal. All personal conflicts are behind," Coach Hristo Bonev told a news conference on Thursday.
Yordan Lechkov from France's Marseille and Lyuboslav Penev from Spain's Compostela also joined in the training session after missing the previous qualifiers by backing Stoichkov's boycott.
Stoichkov, who plays for Barcelona, quit the team last year, demanding the resignation of soccer union chiefs who had axed former head coach Dimitar Penev.

Spain, who head group six by one point from Yugoslavia, have been hit by injuries to two Barcelona defenders, Sergi Barjuan and Miguel Angel Nadal, before their Sunday match against the Czech Republic.
Athletic Bilbao striker Ismael Urzaiz and Atletico Madrid utility player Juan Lopez have taken their places, leaving the side dangerously short of first-rank defenders.
"The Czechs play on the counter-attack so it's not so important," said Spanish coach Javier Clemente.

The Czechs, whose form has slumped since they reached the European championship final last June, have only an outside chance of qualifying for the finals in France next year but their talented squad could still test the Spanish.

The home squad's preparations have also been hit by rain storms in northern Spain. The weather has not just hit training sessions, it also caused the partial collapse of a ceiling during a news conference given by Clemente.

Belgium, bidding to equal the Netherlands points total at the top of group seven, welcome San Marino. But they would need to win by a record-equalling 17-0 to overtake their neighbours who have a far superior goal difference.

The Belgians will be weakened by the absence of captain and World Cup veteran Enzo Scifo of Monaco, who is dogged by a toe injury and expected to be replaced in the starting line-up by Espanyol's Dominique Lemoine.
Anderlecht defender Olivier Doll is out with a thigh injury and striker Lokonda Mpenza of Mouscron is hampered by a slight thigh strain.
But Fiorentina's Luis Oliveira has almost recovered from an ankle injury and should be fit in time. The Netherlands, who have played one more game than Belgium are not in action at the weekend.
